outputs: AI-generated student essays (instruction-based, refined, continuation writing)
The paper generates essays based on prompts from the ASAP dataset using LLMs, including instruction-based, refined, and continuation writing modes.

changes_made.explanation: Removed redundant 'essay writing' task and simplified output description. Normalized model names to standard capitalization.
Consolidated duplicate metric entries and normalized to standard formatting (title case, removing redundant QWK abbreviation).

Removed all metadata as this question asks specifically about LLMs used AS judges (evaluators), not detectors. The models listed are detection models used for classification, not LLMs evaluating generation quality.

guideline: Annotators were presented with pairs of essays and asked to indicate preference without knowing which was AI-generated or human-written

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated guideline descriptions into a single clear statement. Simplified criteria to 'preference' since the paper only mentions pairwise preference evaluation without specific quality dimensions.

overall_notes: This paper focuses on evaluating AI-generated text detection methods rather than evaluating NLG quality per se. The human evaluation is limited to preference judgments without detailed quality criteria. Automatic metrics primarily measure detection performance rather than text quality. The NLG tasks are essay generation and paraphrase generation for evasion purposes.
